\n <div><h2>Как устроено зрение</h2:
How vision works

Optics. Light is refracted by the cornea (about 43 diopters) and the lens (about 19 at rest). The retina receives a reduced, inverted image. To look at something close, the ciliary muscle slackens the zonular fibers and the lens becomes more convex: this is accommodation.

Retina. About 120 million rods (twilight vision) and about 6 million cones (color and detail). Retinal neurons compress their signals, and roughly 1 million optic nerve fibers carry them to the brain.

The chiasm

In the chiasm, fibers from the nasal halves of the retinas cross to the opposite side, while fibers from the temporal halves continue straight on. That is why the right hemisphere receives the left half of the visual field from both eyes, and the left hemisphere receives the right half. The colors show it: turquoise fibers carry the left field, lilac fibers the right.

Further on

The optic tract ends in the lateral geniculate body of the thalamus. From there the optic radiation curves around the lateral ventricle and reaches the primary visual cortex (V1) of the occipital lobe, along the banks of the calcarine sulcus. Every point of the visual field has its own place in the cortex.

What is accurate here

  • The course of the four fiber bundles and the visual field defects caused by damage to the optic nerve, chiasm and tract.
  • The direction of the focusing error in myopia, hyperopia and presbyopia.

Simplifications

  • Rays inside the eye are drawn schematically, without an exact calculation of refraction.
  • The position of the geniculate body is labeled approximately.
  • The signal wave is greatly slowed down.

<b>Дендриты</b> — ветвящиеся входы нейро: Dendrites are the branching inputs of the neuron. They receive most of its synapses. Dendrites also contain Nissl substance and mitochondria: proteins are made right on the spot.
<b>Дендритные шипики</b> — выросты до 3: Dendritic spines are protrusions up to 3 µm long, each with a single synapse on its head. Spines grow, change shape and disappear during learning: this is synaptic plasticity you can actually see.
<b>Ядро</b> хранит ДНК. Через крупные по: The nucleus stores DNA. RNA molecules leave through its large pores and travel to the ribosomes. A neuron's nucleus is large and pale because its genes are very active.
<b>Ядрышко</b> — тёмный участок ядра, зд: The nucleolus is a dark region of the nucleus where ribosomes are assembled. In neurons it is especially prominent.
<b>Субстанция Ниссля</b> (тигроид) — сто: Nissl substance (tigroid substance) consists of stacks of rough ER packed with ribosomes. A neuron is constantly making proteins: channels, receptors, enzymes for transmitter synthesis. Franz Nissl saw these clumps by staining tissue with methylene blue. There is no Nissl substance in the axon hillock.
<b>Аппарат Гольджи</b> дорабатывает белк: The Golgi apparatus finishes processing proteins from the ER and buds off vesicles, including the transmitter-filled vesicles for synapses.
<b>Митохондрии</b> окисляют глюкозу и да: Mitochondria oxidize glucose and produce ATP. A neuron depends heavily on them: without oxygen it survives only a few minutes.
<b>Лизосомы</b> переваривают отслужившие: Lysosomes digest worn-out proteins and membranes. A neuron lives as long as the person does, so clearing out waste is especially important for it.
<b>Нейрофиламенты и микротрубочки</b> де: Neurofilaments and microtubules hold the shape of the neuron's processes and act as rails: motor proteins carry vesicles and mitochondria along them in both directions through the axon (bright dots).
<b>Аксонный холмик</b> — место возникнов: The axon hillock is where the action potential arises. It has the highest density of sodium channels and the lowest threshold. All signals from the dendrites and the cell body are summed right here.
<b>Миелиновая оболочка</b> — слоистая му: The myelin sheath is a layered wrapping made from the membrane of a glial cell (a Schwann cell in the periphery, an oligodendrocyte in the brain). Between the wrappings are the nodes of Ranvier, and the impulse jumps from node to node.
<b>Синапсы</b> — окончания чужих аксонов: Synapses are the endings of other neurons' axons on the dendrites, spines and cell body. Orange ones excite, blue ones inhibit. A single cortical neuron has thousands of them.
<b>Один синапс.</b> Медиатор открыл кана: A single synapse. The transmitter has opened channels, and a small wave of depolarization (an EPSP, orange) runs along the dendrite toward the hillock. It fades on the way: only +3–5 mV reaches the hillock, far from threshold. A single synapse usually cannot trigger an impulse.
<b>Пространственная суммация.</b> Восемь: Spatial summation. Eight synapses in different places fire almost simultaneously. Their waves add up at the hillock and cross the threshold (≈ −55 mV): an action potential is born and travels down the axon, jumping between the nodes of Ranvier.
<b>Временная суммация.</b> Один и тот же: Temporal summation. The same synapse fires six times in a row. Each new wave arrives before the previous one has faded, and they add up to threshold.
<b>Торможение.</b> Тот же залп из восьми: Inhibition. The same volley from eight synapses, but at the same moment inhibitory synapses right at the hillock fire too (blue, GABA). The inhibitory current cancels the excitation exactly where the fate of the impulse is decided, and no action potential arises.
Нейрон в разрезе. Нажмите на любую часть: A neuron in section. Click any part of the cell or choose it from the list. Bottom right is the axon hillock potential: try summation.
Тело нейрона в разрезе: ядро, субстанция: The neuron cell body in section: nucleus, Nissl substance, Golgi apparatus, mitochondria and cytoskeletal filaments. Signals from synapses converge on the axon hillock, where it is decided whether an impulse will fire.
\n <div><h2>Что внутри нейрона</h2>:
What is inside a neuron

Inside, a neuron is built like a typical cell: a nucleus with DNA, from whose large pores RNA emerges; ribosomes on the channels of the ER; a Golgi apparatus that buds off transmitter-filled vesicles; mitochondria that oxidize glucose and produce ATP.

What makes a neuron special

There are a great many ribosomes: a neuron synthesizes proteins all the time, so its rough ER is gathered into clumps, the tigroid, or Nissl substance. In glial cells the tigroid is barely visible. The myelin around the axon is the layered membrane of a glial cell. Thousands of synaptic contacts reach the dendrites and cell body.

How an impulse is born

Each synapse produces a small shift in potential that fades along the way. An impulse arises only if the sum of these shifts at the axon hillock crosses the threshold: this is how spatial and temporal summation work. Inhibitory synapses sit closest to the hillock and can cancel even strong excitation.

What is accurate here

  • There is no tigroid in the axon hillock, and the cytoskeletal filaments converge into the axon.
  • Excitatory synapses on spines, dendrites and the cell body; inhibitory ones at the hillock.
  • The EPSP fades with distance, and the threshold is about −55 mV.

Simplifications

  • Time is slowed down about 50-fold.
  • Organelles and ribosomes are larger than to scale; there are hundreds of times fewer synapses than on a real neuron.

<b>Оболочки мозга</b> — переход от твёрд: The meninges are the transition from hard bone to delicate nervous tissue. Outermost is the dura mater: as tough as flexible plastic; between the hemispheres it forms the falx cerebri, and above the cerebellum the tentorium. Beneath it lies the arachnoid mater: a sponge of connective-tissue cells that cushions blows. Deeper still are the subarachnoid space with CSF and the pia mater with its blood vessels, fused to the surface of the brain.
<b>Желудочки</b> выросли из канала нервн: The ventricles developed from the canal of the neural tube. The telencephalon has two lateral ventricles (I and II), the diencephalon the narrow third ventricle, and the hindbrain the fourth ventricle, shaped like a four-sided pyramid with a rhomboid floor. The third and fourth ventricles are connected by the narrow cerebral aqueduct of the midbrain. The red beads are the choroid plexuses, which secrete CSF.
<b>Ток ликвора</b>: сплетения боковых же: CSF flow: choroid plexuses of the lateral ventricles → interventricular foramina → third ventricle → cerebral aqueduct → fourth ventricle. From there, through the foramina of Magendie and Luschka, CSF passes into the subarachnoid space, bathes the outside of the brain and is absorbed into a venous sinus through the arachnoid granulations. It carries ions, nutrients and regulatory molecules.
<b>Гидроцефалия.</b> Водопровод перекрыт: Hydrocephalus. The cerebral aqueduct is blocked (this can happen with birth injury, a tumor or inflammation). CSF is still being secreted but cannot drain: the lateral and third ventricles swell and press on the brain from the inside, and intracranial pressure rises. It is treated with a shunt that drains the CSF away.
Внутри мозга — система полостей с ликвор: Inside the brain is a system of cavities filled with CSF; outside are three membranes. They nourish and protect the brain and serve as convenient landmarks in anatomy.
\n <div><h2>Желудочки мозга</h2>\n:
The ventricles of the brain

It all starts with the canal of the neural tube: in the hindbrain it widens into the fourth ventricle, in the diencephalon into the third, and in the hemispheres into the lateral ventricles (I and II), with extensions into the frontal and temporal lobes. The third ventricle is narrow and slit-like and reaches almost to the pituitary gland. Between the third and fourth ventricles runs the cerebral aqueduct of the midbrain, similar in size to the central canal of the spinal cord. The floor of the fourth ventricle is the rhomboid fossa, with the cerebellum lying above it.

CSF

The total volume of the system is about 150 mL. CSF flows slowly from the lateral ventricles to the fourth and emerges onto the surface of the brain. If the flow is disrupted, for example by a birth injury, intracranial pressure rises and hydrocephalus may develop.

Meninges

The dura, arachnoid and pia mater cover both the brain and the spinal cord. In the spine, between the dura and the bone, there is the epidural space: this is where anesthetic is injected during epidural anesthesia.

What is accurate here

  • The shape and connections of the ventricles: the lateral ventricles with their inferior horns, the foramina, the slit of the third ventricle, the aqueduct, the pyramid of the fourth ventricle, the central canal.
  • The route of CSF and the site of its absorption into the sinus.
  • The order of the meninges and the folds of the dura: the falx and the tentorium.

Simplifications

  • The thickness of the meninges is greatly exaggerated.
  • CSF flow is sped up: in reality CSF is renewed 3–4 times a day.

Поперечный срез спинного мозга (спинная: A cross-section of the spinal cord (dorsal side up). The gray matter looks like a butterfly: the thin posterior horns almost reach the surface, the thick anterior horns do not, and the lateral horns lie between them. Around it is the white matter with its tracts. Sensory fibers enter through the posterior root, which carries a swelling, the spinal (dorsal root) ganglion, with pseudounipolar neurons. The axons of motor neurons and autonomic neurons leave through the anterior root. Below lies the sympathetic trunk with its white and gray rami.
Tracts, numbered on the section. Blue and green are ascending, sensory: 1 fasciculus gracilis (from the legs), 2 fasciculus cuneatus (from the arms), 3 and 4 spinocerebellar, 5 and 6 spinothalamic (pain, temperature). Red and orange are descending: 7 and 8 pyramidal (voluntary movement), 9–13 the ancient extrapyramidal system: the vestibulospinal, reticulospinal, rubrospinal, olivospinal and tectospinal tracts.
<b>Коленный рефлекс</b> — моносинаптичес: The knee-jerk reflex is a monosynaptic arc. The hammer suddenly stretches the quadriceps, and the muscle spindle fires. The impulse runs along the sensory fiber, through the ganglion and the posterior root, straight to a motor neuron in the anterior horn: just one synapse. The motor neuron responds and the muscle contracts. This is the fastest reflex: it maintains posture when a load suddenly stretches a muscle.
<b>Отдёргивание</b> — полисинаптический: The withdrawal reflex is polysynaptic. Prick → pain ending → ganglion → interneuron of the posterior horn → interneuron of the intermediate zone → flexor motor neurons of the same and neighboring segments. The stronger the pain, the more muscles are recruited. At the same time the signal crosses to the other side and ascends to the thalamus (red tail going up): that is how we become aware of the pain only after we have already pulled the hand away.
<b>Мозг тормозит рефлекс.</b> На вставоч: The brain inhibits the reflex. Axons from the brain (blue signal from above) reach the interneuron of the intermediate zone. If the brain manages to send an inhibitory signal in time, the hand is not pulled away: this is how we hold still while blood is taken from a finger. The knee-jerk reflex has no such interneuron, so it cannot be suppressed.
<b>Вегетативная дуга</b> из двух нейроно: An autonomic arc of two neurons. A preganglionic neuron of the lateral horn sends its axon through the anterior root and the white ramus to a sympathetic ganglion. There a postganglionic neuron sends its axon along the gray ramus back into the nerve, to blood vessels, sweat glands and the muscles of the hair follicles. Sympathetic neurons are found only in the thoracic and upper lumbar segments.
<b>31 сегмент</b> — 31 «этаж» тела: 8 ше: 31 segments are the 31 “floors” of the body: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and one coccygeal. Each gives off a pair of nerves. The spine grows faster than the cord, so in an adult the spinal cord ends at the second lumbar vertebra, and below it the roots run downward as the cauda equina. The enlargements in the cervical and lumbar regions control the arms and legs. A lumbar puncture is done below the end of the cord, in the lumbar cistern.
Трубка из нервной ткани в позвоночном ка: A tube of nervous tissue in the vertebral canal: 31 segments, reflex arcs and the tracts that link the body with the brain.
\n <div><h2>Как устроен спинной моз:
How the spinal cord is built

It is 42–45 cm long and weighs 34–38 g, with a canal about 1 mm wide inside. It contains 13.5 million neurons, and only 3% of them are efferent (motor and autonomic neurons); the remaining 97% are interneurons. The posterior roots are the sensory inputs, the anterior roots the motor and autonomic outputs. The roots, ganglia and nerves belong to the peripheral nervous system.

Gray matter

Sensory signals are relayed in the posterior horns: the marginal zone, the spongy zone and the substantia gelatinosa (pain), the nucleus proprius, and Clarke's thoracic nucleus (proprioception). The lateral horns hold the sympathetic centers of the thoracic and upper lumbar segments and the main “computing center”, the intermediomedial nucleus. The anterior horns hold the motor neurons: the lateral nuclei control distal muscles (the fingers), the medial nuclei the trunk. Bror Rexed divided the gray matter into 10 laminae.

White matter

The posterior columns carry skin and muscle sensation without a relay in the spinal cord: the first synapse is only in the medulla. The spinocerebellar tracts are even faster. Pain and temperature travel more slowly, along the spinothalamic tracts, which cross at their own segment. The pyramidal tract: 80% of it crosses at the border with the brain, the remaining 20% at the level of its own segment.

What is accurate here

  • The shape of the section: the posterior horns thinner and longer, the anterior horns thicker; the posterior sulcus and the deep anterior fissure.
  • The monosynaptic knee-jerk reflex and the polysynaptic withdrawal reflex with its ascending branch to the thalamus.
  • The two-neuron autonomic arc through the white and gray rami.
  • The compressed segments and the cauda equina below the second lumbar vertebra.

Simplifications

  • Time is slowed down about 80-fold: a real knee-jerk reflex takes about 20–25 ms.
  • The vertebra is simplified; the muscle and skin are moved close to the spinal cord.

<b>II — зрительный нерв</b> идёт от сетч: II — the optic nerve runs from the retina to the diencephalon and forms a crossing, the chiasm. By origin it is, like the olfactory nerve, a CNS tract rather than a true nerve.

<b>IV — блоковый нерв</b> — единственный: IV — the trochlear nerve is the only one that leaves the dorsal side of the brainstem (from below the inferior colliculi) and wraps around it from the side. It controls a single eye muscle.

<b>VIII — преддверно-улитковый нерв</b>: VIII — the vestibulocochlear nerve emerges together with the facial nerve. In humans it is purely sensory: hearing from the cochlea and balance from the vestibule.

<b>X — блуждающий нерв</b> — главный пар: X — the vagus nerve is the body's main parasympathetic nerve. It supplies the organs of the chest and abdomen, receives information from them, and controls the upper esophagus and the vocal cords.

\n <div><h2>Как их запомнить</h2>\n:
How to remember them

Sensory: I, II, VIII: smell, vision, the inner ear (hearing and balance). Motor: IV, VI, XII. Motor with parasympathetic fibers: III and XI. Mixed: V, VII, IX, X: in their set of functions they are closest to spinal nerves.

Where they emerge

I enters the telencephalon, II the diencephalon. III and IV emerge from the midbrain (IV is the only one on the dorsal side). V is associated with the pons. VI, VII and VIII emerge at the border of the pons and the medulla, IX–XII from the medulla.

Evolution

The set did not appear all at once: fish still lack some of the nerves, amphibians and reptiles lack the accessory nerve XI, and the full set is found in birds and mammals. The medulla and pons retain the plan of the spinal cord: sensory nuclei lie laterally, motor nuclei medially, and parasympathetic nuclei between them.

  • Where the nerves emerge on the underside of the brain.
  • Classification by function and the direction of the signal.
  • The ganglion and three branches of the trigeminal nerve.

Simplifications

  • The course of the nerves inside the skull is simplified.

The basis (red) is white matter: the pyramids of the medulla, the bulge of the pons, the cerebral peduncles of the midbrain, the tracts running up and down. The tegmentum (green) lies beneath the floor of the fourth ventricle and the aqueduct: the cranial nerve nuclei, the reticular formation, the ascending lemnisci. It holds the vital centers: the respiratory center (every breath is started here; blue waves travel to the diaphragm) and the vasomotor center (the rate and force of the heartbeat, the diameter of blood vessels). Here too are the centers for swallowing, coughing, sneezing, vomiting and blinking, and the system that wakes up the cortex. Bottom right: the rhythms of the centers.

The medial lemniscus (blue) carries skin and muscle sensation: the first synapse is in the nuclei of the gracile and cuneate fasciculi, then it crosses and ascends to the thalamus. That is why the left hemisphere controls the right half of the body and feels it.
<b>Ориентировочный рефлекс</b> — «рефлек: The orienting reflex is Pavlov's “what is it?” reflex. Novelty-detector neurons in the superior colliculi compare the picture with the one from 0.3 s ago. A flash at the edge of the visual field → superior colliculi → tectospinal tract → neck motor neurons: the head turns toward the source before we are even aware of what happened. The inferior colliculi respond to new sounds in the same way.
<b>Болезнь Паркинсона.</b> Дофаминовые н: Parkinson's disease. The dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra die, and almost no dopamine reaches the striatum anymore. The result is tremor, stiffness (rigidity) and difficulty starting a movement (akinesia). The black color of the substantia nigra comes from melanin; in the disease it turns pale.
Продолговатый мозг, мост и средний мозг: The medulla oblongata, pons and midbrain are ancient parts of the brain shared by all vertebrates. They hold the centers of breathing and heartbeat, sleep and wakefulness, and all the pathways between the brain and the body.
\n <div><h2>Из чего состоит ствол</:
What the brainstem is made of

The medulla oblongata resembles a truncated cone about 4 cm long (from 1.5 to 2.5 cm wide). In front are the pyramids and olives; behind is the floor of the fourth ventricle, the rhomboid fossa. The pons is almost square, 2.5–3 cm; it becomes a separate structure only in mammals, together with the cortex and cerebellum: through the pontine nuclei the cortex sends copies of motor programs to the cerebellum. The midbrain is small but important: the corpora quadrigemina, the aqueduct with the periaqueductal gray, the red nucleus and the substantia nigra.

Genes

The parts of the brainstem are laid down by homeotic genes: Pax, Otx2, Wnt1, Gbx2, Fgf8, Shh, Hox. In a newer classification, the medulla and pons are assembled from 11 stereotyped units.

Evolution

In fish the main integrative center is the midbrain. In humans the brainstem is far lighter than the cerebellum and the hemispheres, but without it breathing, the heartbeat and wakefulness itself are impossible.

  • The shape of the brainstem: pyramids, olives, the bulge of the pons, peduncles, corpora quadrigemina, rhomboid fossa.
  • The division into basis, tegmentum and tectum.
  • The positions of the locus coeruleus, raphe nuclei, substantia nigra, ventral tegmental area and red nucleus.
  • The decussation of the pyramids and of the medial lemniscus.

<b>Непроизвольное внимание.</b> На краю: Involuntary attention. Something moved at the edge of the visual field. The corpora quadrigemina report this to the thalamus, and it opens a “green corridor” for the visual stream into the cortex: attention switches by itself, even if we were busy with something else.
<b>Жажда.</b> Нейроны <b>супраоптических: Thirst. Neurons of the supraoptic nuclei sense that the blood has become too concentrated. Their axons run down the stalk straight into the posterior pituitary and release vasopressin into the blood. The kidneys start to reclaim water, and the person looks for something to drink.
<b>Стресс.</b> Паравентрикулярные ядра в: Stress. The paraventricular nuclei release corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) into the portal vessels. These carry it to the anterior lobe of the pituitary, which releases ACTH into the blood. ACTH reaches the adrenal glands, and they secrete cortisol. The “fight or flight” decision is made by the amygdala and carried out by the posterior zones of the hypothalamus.
<b>Биологические часы.</b> <b>Супрахиазм: The biological clock. The suprachiasmatic nuclei lie right above the optic chiasm and learn the overall light level from the retina. When it gets dark, they signal the pineal gland, which releases melatonin, a hormone that calms many of the body's systems. This is how the daily rhythm is maintained.
<b>Окситоцин.</b> Паравентрикулярные ядр: Oxytocin. The paraventricular nuclei synthesize oxytocin and send it along their axons to the posterior pituitary. It triggers uterine contractions during childbirth and milk ejection, and takes part in attachment and caregiving; the centers of parental behavior lie in the anterior zones of the hypothalamus.
<b>Таламус</b> — информационный фильтр н: The thalamus is an information filter at the entrance to the cortex. Through it pass vision (lateral geniculate body), hearing (medial geniculate body), skin and muscle sensation (ventrobasal complex), motor programs from the cerebellum and basal ganglia, and signals of memory and emotion. Smell is the only exception. Choose what to pay attention to: the thalamus will open a “green corridor” for one stream and dampen the others. The inhibitory “shell” is the reticular nucleus.
<b>Гипоталамус</b> — нижняя часть промеж: The hypothalamus is the lower part of the diencephalon, with more than 30 pairs of nuclei. It holds the centers of hunger and thirst, sexual and parental behavior, fear and aggression, sleep and the biological clock. Together with the pituitary gland it controls all the endocrine glands: the posterior lobe releases hormones made in hypothalamic neurons, and the anterior lobe obeys the hypothalamus's releasing and inhibiting hormones (liberins and statins). Try the experiments.
Таламус решает, какая информация попадёт: The thalamus decides which information reaches the cortex. The hypothalamus monitors the body's needs and controls hormones through the pituitary gland.
\n <div><h2>Промежуточный мозг</h2>:
The diencephalon

It develops from the forebrain vesicle: the lower wall gives rise to the hypothalamus (the most ancient part), the side walls to the thalamus, the upper wall to the epithalamus with the pineal gland, and the back wall to the metathalamus (the geniculate bodies). All these structures grew from the dorsal plate of the neural tube, so they contain no motor neurons, only relay neurons and interneurons.

Thalamus

Neuroanatomists distinguish about 40 nuclei, neurosurgeons up to 80. Specific nuclei pass sensory and motor signals to the cortex with a precise map of the body, the retina or the cochlea. Nonspecific nuclei set the overall tone of the cortex and work in the sleep–wake system. Associative nuclei (the pulvinar, the dorsal nuclei) are connected with the frontal and parietal cortex and help recognize complex images. In chronic pain, neurosurgeons make precise lesions in certain thalamic networks.

Hypothalamus

The anterior nuclei produce parasympathetic effects (slowing of the heart, constriction of the pupil), the posterior nuclei sympathetic ones (dilation of the pupil, a rise in blood pressure). The medial zones handle the motivation to eat and drink, the anterior zones sexual and parental behavior, the posterior zones fear and aggression. The suprachiasmatic nuclei are the biological clock.

What is accurate here

  • The location of the main thalamic nuclei and their links to cortical areas.
  • The reticular nucleus as the inhibitory shell of the thalamus.
  • The posterior pituitary receives axons from the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei; the anterior pituitary receives releasing hormones through the portal vessels.
  • The pathway “suprachiasmatic nuclei → pineal gland → melatonin”.

Simplifications

  • The cortex is shown as a dome; the thalamus and hypothalamus are enlarged.
  • Hormones are drawn as glowing particles, and time is compressed.

<b>Хвостатое ядро</b> — С-образное, лежи: The caudate nucleus is C-shaped and lies above and lateral to the thalamus. Its head bulges into the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle, its body lies in the ventricle's wall, and its tail runs into the temporal lobe toward the amygdala. The brain has to curve its structures into arcs, following the rounded shape of the skull.
<b>Скорлупа</b> вместе с хвостатым ядром: The putamen and the caudate nucleus form a single structure, the striatum (corpus striatum): sections show alternating stripes of gray and white matter. Its main job is movement and motor skills.
<b>Бледный шар</b> (наружная и внутрення: The globus pallidus (external and internal segments) is an inhibitory “filter”: it constantly holds back the thalamus and keeps unwanted motor programs from starting. Putamen + globus pallidus = lentiform nucleus.
<b>Ограда</b> — тонкий слой серого вещес: The claustrum is a thin layer of gray matter between the putamen and the insular cortex.
<b>Миндалевидный комплекс</b> лежит в гл: The amygdaloid complex lies deep in the temporal lobe. It is the part of the basal ganglia linked to emotion: fear, anxiety, the “fight or flight” choice.
<b>Прилежащее ядро</b> (вентральный стри: The nucleus accumbens (ventral striatum) is the center of the reward system. Together with the amygdala, the ventral tegmental area and the hypothalamus, it belongs to the limbic system of needs, motivation and emotion.
<b>Таламус</b> — не базальный ганглий, н: The thalamus is not a basal ganglion, but it is their main partner: the basal ganglia influence the cortex through its ventral anterior nucleus.
<b>Базальные ганглии</b> — скопления сер: The basal ganglia are clusters of gray matter deep in the hemispheres. About 80% of their neurons (caudate nucleus, putamen, globus pallidus), together with the cerebellum, premotor cortex, subthalamus and substantia nigra, control movement: motor learning, skills, assembling movements into a program. About 20% (nucleus accumbens and amygdala) work in the limbic system. Click a nucleus or run the motor loop.
<b>Белое вещество полушарий.</b> <b>Прое: The white matter of the hemispheres. Projection fibers (red) connect the cortex with lower parts of the nervous system: all of them pass through the internal capsule. Commissural fibers (blue) connect the hemispheres: the corpus callosum (the “new” commissure), the anterior commissure (the “ancient” one, about 3 million fibers, olfactory areas) and the hippocampal commissure. Association fibers (green) connect cortical areas within a hemisphere: the superior longitudinal fasciculus links the frontal cortex with the parietal, temporal and occipital cortex, and the inferior one links the temporal with the occipital cortex.
<b>Фронтальный срез</b>. Снаружи — кора: Coronal section. On the outside is the cortex with its sulci and gyri, beneath it the white matter. At the top is the corpus callosum, with the lateral ventricles below it. Medially lie the caudate nucleus and the thalamus; laterally, beyond the internal capsule, the putamen and globus pallidus; farther out, the thin claustrum and the insular cortex deep in the lateral sulcus. At the bottom are the amygdala in the temporal lobe and the hypothalamus beside the third ventricle.
<b>Двигательная петля.</b> Кора предлага: The motor loop. The cortex proposes a movement → signal to the striatum (orange) → the striatum inhibits the internal globus pallidus (blue) → the globus pallidus stops inhibiting the thalamus → the thalamus “lets” the program back through to the motor cortex. Dopamine from the substantia nigra (yellow) makes this launch easier. This is how the right movement is selected from many possible ones.
<b>Петля при болезни Паркинсона.</b> Доф: The loop in Parkinson's disease. There is no dopamine: the striatum barely inhibits the globus pallidus, which keeps pressing on the thalamus, and the program hardly reaches the cortex. Movements are hard to start, and stiffness and tremor appear.
Под корой — белое вещество и ядра базаль: Beneath the cortex lie the white matter and the nuclei of the basal ganglia. They assemble individual movements into programs and, together with the limbic system, decide what we need.
\n <div><h2>Конечный мозг</h2>\n:
The telencephalon

The largest part of the brain, it covers all the others, and the longitudinal fissure divides it into two hemispheres. On the outside is the cortex with its sulci and gyri, beneath it the white matter, and deep inside the basal ganglia: the caudate nucleus, putamen, globus pallidus, claustrum and amygdala.

What the parts are called

Putamen + globus pallidus = lentiform nucleus. Caudate + lentiform = corpus striatum (striatum). The dorsal striatum is the caudate and lentiform nuclei; the ventral striatum is the nucleus accumbens.

Basal ganglia and cerebellum

The cerebellum remembers how to perform a particular movement quickly and precisely (a single step in a dance). The basal ganglia assemble movements into a long program (the whole dance with its transitions between figures). In both cases synaptic plasticity is at work.

What is accurate here

  • The C-shaped caudate nucleus along the lateral ventricle, with its tail near the amygdala.
  • The order of layers on the section: internal capsule, globus pallidus, putamen, claustrum, insula.
  • The three types of white matter fibers.
  • The scheme of the motor loop “cortex — striatum — globus pallidus — thalamus — cortex”.

Simplifications

  • The brain is a simplified model, and the nuclei are shown as smooth bodies.
  • In reality there are millions of fibers; here there are dozens.

<b>Поле 4</b> — прецентральная извилина,: Area 4 is the precentral gyrus, the primary motor cortex. It contains the giant Betz pyramidal cells, whose axons form the pyramidal tract. It has a precise topography: each part controls its own muscles.
<b>Поле 6</b> — премоторная область, вто: Area 6 is the premotor area, a secondary motor field. Here the overall program is broken down into individual movements.
<b>Поле 8</b> — верхняя лобная извилина,: Area 8, in the superior frontal gyrus, controls eye movements.
<b>Префронтальная кора</b> (поле 9 и сос: The prefrontal cortex (area 9 and neighboring areas) holds the most general motor program: goals, plans, decisions. The flow runs “top-down”: prefrontal cortex → areas 6 and 8 → area 4 → muscles.
<b>Зона Брока</b> (поля 44 и 45, нижняя: Broca's area (areas 44 and 45, inferior frontal gyrus) is the motor center of speech: it drives the motor side of speaking. In right-handers it is in the left hemisphere.
<b>Зона Брока</b> (поля 44 и 45) — мотор: Broca's area (areas 44 and 45) is the motor center of speech. When it is damaged, a person understands speech but speaks with difficulty.
<b>Поле 47</b> — по классической схеме с: Area 47 is linked to singing in the classical scheme.
<b>Поля 3, 1, 2</b> — постцентральная из: Areas 3, 1, 2 form the postcentral gyrus: skin, muscle and pain sensation. Area 3 is primary: it receives almost unprocessed signals from the thalamic projection nuclei.
<b>Поле 43</b> — вкусовая кора, у остров: Area 43 is the gustatory cortex, next to the insula.
<b>Поля 5 и 7</b> — вторичные чувствител: Areas 5 and 7 are the secondary sensory fields of the superior parietal lobule: individual sensations are combined into an image.
<b>Поле 7</b> — верхняя теменная долька,: Area 7 is the superior parietal lobule, a secondary and partly associative field: the body in space.
<b>Надкраевая извилина</b> (40) — ассоци: The supramarginal gyrus (40) is associative parietal cortex: it combines streams from different senses. Damage to tertiary fields impairs complex recognition.
<b>Угловая извилина</b> (39) — зрительны: The angular gyrus (39) handles the visual images of words and reading. It is part of the occipito-temporo-parietal association area.
<b>Поле 17</b> — первичная зрительная ко: Area 17 is the primary visual cortex, mostly on the medial surface along the banks of the calcarine sulcus. Neighboring columns respond to lines of different orientations.
<b>Поле 18</b> — вторичное зрительное: и: Area 18 is secondary visual cortex: lines are assembled into an image; in the classical scheme, written language.
<b>Поле 19</b> — вторичное зрительное, з: Area 19 is secondary visual cortex, memory for images.
<b>Поле 41</b> — первичная слуховая кора: Area 41 is the primary auditory cortex (the transverse gyri deep in the lateral sulcus): auditory perception.
<b>Поле 42</b> — вторичная слуховая кора: Area 42 is secondary auditory cortex: sound discrimination.
<b>Зона Вернике</b> (задняя часть поля 2: Wernicke's area (the posterior part of area 22, superior temporal gyrus) is the sensory center of speech: the auditory images of words. Area 22 is also involved in orienting to sound and in musical hearing.
<b>Средняя и нижняя височные извилины</b: The middle and inferior temporal gyri: recognition of objects and faces, associative temporal cortex.
<b>Поле 37</b> — затылочно-височная обла: Area 37 is the occipitotemporal region; in the classical scheme it is linked to voluntary speech.
<b>Височный полюс</b> (38) связан с лимб: The temporal pole (38) is connected with the limbic system and emotional memory.
<b>Поясная извилина</b> (поля 24, 25 и с: The cingulate gyrus (areas 24, 25 and neighboring areas) detects mismatches and errors; it is part of the limbic lobe.
